challengesDone: The stages that make up the game, challenges that the student must fulfill within each game.
movesToCompleteEachGame: Moves the student must complete within each game (Exercises/Questions)
gamesAccessed: Games the student accessed, may have completed or not
progressBasedOnGamesCompletedByStudent: Calculates progress based on the number of games completed by the student.
performanceBasedOnStudentMistakesAndSucc: Calculates performance based on students' mistakes and successes in their challenges (moves).
educationColorKeyLegend:
¹The green color is anchored in Goal 3 of Todos Pela Educação, which states that 70% of students should demonstrate adequate learning, and the yellow color signifies that it is still slightly below that percentage. Meanwhile, the orange color suggests that it is considered unsuccessful if less than 50% of students demonstrate adequate learning. Finally, the red color illustrates that the majority of students do not exhibit a good level of learning.
Source: Saeb, INEP

chooseBookToWorkOn: Choose which book you want to work on
noActiveMissions: The class currently has no active missions.
individualGameDescription: The individual game can be played by each child, in groups, and/or the teacher can play on their screen with the entire class.
collectiveGameDescription: The collective game offers two screens with complementary interactions, one for the teacher and one for the student.
mixedGameDescription: In this area, there are individual and collective games. Therefore, organize with the class the experiences of each game.
simultaneousPlay: Students and teachers should play simultaneously.
recommendationMobileComputer: We recommend that you carry out the activity through the mobile or computer application.
playSimultaneouslyInstructions: To play simultaneously, you must share the screen online or project it in the classroom.

expandGameTheme: Expand the game theme by relating it to other school experiences.

learningRightsExplanation: The League of Owlets, in its set of games, explores and exercises, at different levels, all Learning Rights proposed by BNCC, so that Living Together, Playing, Participating, Exploring, Expressing, and Knowing Oneself are present through interactions in the games, enriching relationships in the teaching and learning process.
howToPlayExplanation: How to play is explained when the student clicks on the question mark (?) in the game
trackActiveMissionReports: Track the reports of active missions

moduleTooltip.Islands: Environments where students can freely explore Educacross games distributed across 11 scenarios.
moduleTooltip.Explore: In this module, students can freely explore Educacross games categorized by age group. The Explore module can be configured by the class teacher, who enables access to games according to the appropriate school years for the class.
moduleTooltip.BookMissions: Sets of games selected by the Educacross pedagogical team in conjunction with the teaching material. Unlike the Teaching System module, games in this category can be customized by the teacher, and the same missions can be enabled multiple times.
moduleTooltip.CustomMissions: Set of games selected by the teacher for the entire class, groups, or for an individual student with pedagogical intent.
moduleTooltip.EducacrossMissions: Sets of games suggested by Educacross that cover the main skills of the BNCC (National Curricular Common Base) and other assessment matrices.
moduleTooltip.SpecialMissions: Sets of games suggested and shared by teachers using the platform.
moduleTooltip.SuggestGuide: Set of games automatically suggested by Educacross based on the selection of an initial game chosen by the teacher.
moduleTooltip.EducationSystems: Sets of games selected by the Educacross pedagogical team in conjunction with the teaching material of the Educational System.
moduleTooltip.StudentTraining: Sets of games suggested by Educacross that cover the main skills of the BNCC and other assessment matrices that can be enabled and disabled by the student's guardians.
moduleTooltip.MissionsTraining: Set of games automatically suggested by Educacross with the aim of training the student's skills in each thematic area of knowledge, minimizing the learning gap in specific competencies.
moduleTooltip.SuperChallenge: The Super Challenge is a seasonal module composed of an initial diagnostic assessment tool that analyzes the individual knowledge level of each student and automatically aligns their needs with the curricular themes of each school year.
moduleTooltip.Evaluations: Digital assessment with multiple-choice questions: generates a general performance report for education networks, schools, classes, and students.
moduleTooltip.Events: Exclusive program that presents the student's progress at each stage, delivering new challenges progressively. This module provides reports for networks, schools, and parents.
moduleTooltip.HighFive: Program that promotes experiences of Mathematics in English. The teacher contextualizes the lesson through games.
moduleTooltip.Reports: Data on the platform for student-teacher interaction: engagement, performance according to the BNCC, and national and state assessment matrices.
moduleTooltip.CardReport: Individual student report with access, performance, and progress data in a specific period and module. The report also presents performance by themes of the knowledge areas covered.
moduleTooltip.BookLibrary: Students can explore a collection of books to read and have fun while developing reading skills.
